inputs.root_cause: Event 322's own exact_next_action named product-goal.yaml's own last fully-unaddressed completion invariant -- 'every distribution extracts to an independent repository with preserved canonical source and package digests' -- as untouched for all six formats since Event 315's own self-correction first flagged it. No prior tool in this repository ever copied a format's own source tree OUT of the monorepo and built it there; reproducible_build_gate.py proves two IN-PLACE builds agree, run_package_install_proof.py always builds from src/python/{format}/ inside the monorepo.
inputs.obligation_targeted: Not a SAL-derived obligation -- product-goal.yaml's own separate 'completion_invariants' list, specifically the independent-repository-extraction clause.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: Built tools/certification/independent_repository_extraction_gate.py: copies src/python/{format}/ verbatim into a fresh OS-temp directory with no ancestor relationship to this repository, verifies byte-identical preservation, builds a wheel+sdist from the isolated copy (cwd never REPO_ROOT) and a second from the in-place source at the same pinned epoch, and compares digests. First run for xliff found a genuine DIGEST_MISMATCH -- investigated and found a real build-hygiene bug (a stale setuptools build/ cache silently shipping an orphaned file), fixed the two shared build tools that had the same latent issue, and re-ran to EXTRACTS_INDEPENDENTLY.
inputs.regression_tier: xliff suite plus 6-format regression, mypy --strict, ruff, plus the package-install-proof/reproducible-build tools' own pass/fail verdicts

execution_steps: 1. Re-read product-goal.yaml's own completion_invariants list directly rather than trusting paraphrase: 'Every distribution extracts to an independent repository with preserved canonical source and package digests.' Grepped the whole repo for this exact phrase and related concepts (canonical_source, package_digest) -- found zero dedicated implementation anywhere, confirming this invariant is genuinely, completely untouched.

2. Read the existing reproducible_build_gate.py and build-local-packages.py directly to understand exactly how a format's wheel is built today -- both invoke `python -m build --wheel --sdist --outdir <dist> <source_dir>` where source_dir is src/python/{format}/ INSIDE the monorepo, and neither ever copies that directory elsewhere first. Confirmed each format's own [build-system] backend-path = ['.'] is self-relative (its own _build_backend.py lives inside its own source_dir), meaning the source tree SHOULD be self-contained enough to copy and build in true isolation -- but nothing had ever tested that claim.

3. Wrote tools/certification/independent_repository_extraction_gate.py: copies src/python/{format}/ (excluding build/dist/__pycache__/etc., matching the exact ignore pattern build-local-packages.py already uses) into tempfile.mkdtemp() -- genuinely outside this repository, not merely a subdirectory of .local/ -- computes a full sha256 manifest of both the original and copied tree and asserts they match exactly (the 'preserved canonical source' half), then builds a wheel+sdist from the isolated copy with cwd set to the isolated root (never REPO_ROOT) and a second wheel+sdist from the in-place source at the identical pinned SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, and compares artifact digests (the 'preserved... package digests' half).

4. First run against xliff: source_preserved_byte_identical=true (73/73 files matched exactly) but package_digests_preserved=false -- verdict DIGEST_MISMATCH on exactly one artifact, the wheel (the sdist matched). This was a genuine, unexpected finding, not assumed away.

5. Investigated directly rather than accepting the mismatch as an inherent limitation: extracted both wheels and diffed their contents file-by-file. Found the in-place-built wheel contained ONE extra file the isolated build did not: format_factory/xliff/validation/xliff_core_2.0.xsd. Checked the current src/ tree directly -- that file only exists at validation/schemas/xliff_core_2.0.xsd today, not at the bare validation/ path. Checked src/python/xliff/build/ (setuptools' own local, gitignored build cache) directly and found build/lib/.../validation/xliff_core_2.0.xsd sitting there as an orphaned leftover from before that file moved under schemas/.

6. Root-caused this precisely: setuptools' legacy build_py command incrementally reuses an existing build/lib/ directory rather than clearing it before copying source files in, so a file removed or moved in src/ can survive indefinitely in build/lib/ and get silently bundled into every subsequent wheel built from that checkout, until build/ is manually cleared. Confirmed src/python/*/build/ is gitignored (not tracked, not committed) via git check-ignore, and confirmed every OTHER FF6 format's own build/ directory also has files (ipynb 39, nrrd 22, ora 15, safetensors 23, ubl 155) -- a portfolio-wide risk class, not xliff-specific, though only xliff's own instance was directly confirmed to have caused an actual digest divergence this tick.

7. Fixed the root cause in the two shared tools that build in-place, not just worked around it in the new gate: added a `shutil.rmtree(source_dir / 'build')` guard before the `python -m build` subprocess call in both packaging/python/build-local-packages.py::_build_source() (the real release-build path run_package_install_proof.py uses) and tools/certification/reproducible_build_gate.py::build_once() (which could carry the same staleness across separate script invocations, even though it could not have made ITS OWN two-builds-in-one-run comparison disagree). Applied the identical fix inline in the new gate's own _build() too.

8. Re-ran independent_repository_extraction_gate.py --format xliff: EXTRACTS_INDEPENDENTLY, wheel digest now agrees between isolated and in-place builds (884a7aadde... for both, was a01b50f7d9... contaminated before the fix).

9. Re-ran reproducible_build_gate.py --package-dir src/python/xliff to keep that gate's own recorded digest consistent with the now-corrected wheel content -- still REPRODUCIBLE, new wheel_sha256 884a7aadde... (matches the independent-extraction gate's own digest exactly, cross-confirming both tools agree).

10. Re-ran tools/run_package_install_proof.py --format xliff for the same reason (build-local-packages.py's own output changed) -- still 1/1 PASS, new proof_id/wheel_sha256 recorded, updated installed-wheel-gate.json's own proof_id and added a note documenting why it changed.

11. Fixed 2 mypy --strict errors in the new gate script's own return-type annotations (bare `dict` -> `dict[str, Any]`, needed because the result dict genuinely holds heterogeneous value types read back with .items()/.get()) -- clean, zero ignores. Left the two EXISTING tools' own pre-existing, unrelated mypy issues untouched (tools/ and packaging/ scripts are not in scope for the typing completion-invariant gate, which targets src/python/{format}/ only -- same precedent already established this session for performance_benchmark.py).

12. Ran the full xliff suite (591 passed, unchanged) and the full 6-format regression (3930 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed, unchanged) to confirm none of this tick's tooling fixes altered any product behavior.
